I'll solve this directly by setting up coordinates and computing the intersection.

**Setup.** Place $A_1=(0,0)$, $A_2=(1,0)$, $A_3=(0,1)$, so $[A_1A_2A_3]=\tfrac12$.

The quarter points are:
- $B_1=\tfrac34 A_1+\tfrac14 A_2=(\tfrac14,0)$, $\;C_1=\tfrac14 A_1+\tfrac34 A_2=(\tfrac34,0)$
- $B_2=\tfrac34 A_2+\tfrac14 A_3=(\tfrac34,\tfrac14)$, $\;C_2=\tfrac14 A_2+\tfrac34 A_3=(\tfrac14,\tfrac34)$
- $B_3=\tfrac34 A_3+\tfrac14 A_1=(0,\tfrac34)$, $\;C_3=\tfrac14 A_3+\tfrac34 A_1=(0,\tfrac14)$

**Finding the intersection.** I parametrize each edge and solve for crossings. A half-plane check shows no vertex of either triangle lies inside the other, so the common region is a hexagon bounded by 6 edge-crossing points:

| Crossing | Edges | Point |
|---|---|---|
| $P_1$ | $B_1B_2 \cap C_1C_2$ | $(\tfrac58,\tfrac{3}{16})$ |
| $P_2$ | $B_1B_2 \cap C_3C_1$ | $(\tfrac{9}{20},\tfrac{1}{10})$ |
| $P_3$ | $B_2B_3 \cap C_1C_2$ | $(\tfrac{9}{20},\tfrac{9}{20})$ |
| $P_4$ | $B_2B_3 \cap C_2C_3$ | $(\tfrac{3}{16},\tfrac58)$ |
| $P_5$ | $B_3B_1 \cap C_2C_3$ | $(\tfrac{1}{10},\tfrac{9}{20})$ |
| $P_6$ | $B_3B_1 \cap C_3C_1$ | $(\tfrac{3}{16},\tfrac{3}{16})$ |

**Verification of one point.** $P_1$: on $B_1B_2$ at $t=\tfrac34$: $(\tfrac14+\tfrac38,\tfrac{3}{16})=(\tfrac58,\tfrac{3}{16})$ ✓; on $C_1C_2$ at $s=\tfrac14$: $(\tfrac34-\tfrac18,\tfrac{3}{16})=(\tfrac58,\tfrac{3}{16})$ ✓.

**Tracing the hexagon.** The boundary alternates between edges of the two triangles. Going around:
$$P_1 \xrightarrow{C_1C_2} P_3 \xrightarrow{B_2B_3} P_4 \xrightarrow{C_2C_3} P_5 \xrightarrow{B_3B_1} P_6 \xrightarrow{C_3C_1} P_2 \xrightarrow{B_1B_2} P_1$$

**Area via the Shoelace formula.** With vertices in this cyclic order:

$$\text{Area}=\tfrac12\left|\sum (x_i y_{i+1}-x_{i+1}y_i)\right|$$

Computing each consecutive pair (all over denominator $320$):

- $P_1P_3$: $\tfrac58\cdot\tfrac{9}{20}-\tfrac{9}{20}\cdot\tfrac{3}{16}=\tfrac{90-27}{320}=\tfrac{63}{320}$
- $P_3P_4$: $\tfrac{9}{20}\cdot\tfrac58-\tfrac{3}{16}\cdot\tfrac{9}{20}=\tfrac{90-27}{320}=\tfrac{63}{320}$
- $P_4P_5$: $\tfrac{3}{16}\cdot\tfrac{9}{20}-\tfrac{1}{10}\cdot\tfrac58=\tfrac{27-20}{320}=\tfrac{7}{320}$
- $P_5P_6$: $\tfrac{1}{10}\cdot\tfrac{3}{16}-\tfrac{3}{16}\cdot\tfrac{9}{20}=\tfrac{6-27}{320}=-\tfrac{21}{320}$
- $P_6P_2$: $\tfrac{3}{16}\cdot\tfrac{1}{10}-\tfrac{9}{20}\cdot\tfrac{3}{16}=\tfrac{6-27}{320}=-\tfrac{21}{320}$
- $P_2P_1$: $\tfrac{9}{20}\cdot\tfrac{3}{16}-\tfrac58\cdot\tfrac{1}{10}=\tfrac{27-20}{320}=\tfrac{7}{320}$

$$\text{Sum}=\frac{63+63+7-21-21+7}{320}=\frac{98}{320}$$

$$[\text{hexagon}]=\frac12\cdot\frac{98}{320}=\frac{49}{320}$$

**Final fraction.** Since $[A_1A_2A_3]=\tfrac12$:

$$\frac{[\text{common part}]}{[A_1A_2A_3]}=\frac{49/320}{1/2}=\boxed{\dfrac{49}{160}}$$

- $B_1=\tfrac34 A_1+\tfrac14 A_2=(\tfrac14,0)$, $\;C_1=\tfrac14 A_1+\tfrac34 A_2=(\tfrac34,0)$

**Finding the intersection.** I parametrize each edge and solve for crossings. A half-plane check shows no vertex of either triangle lies inside the other, so the common region is a hexagon bounded by 6 edge-crossing points:

| Crossing | Edges | Point |
|---|---|---|
| $P_1$ | $B_1B_2 \cap C_1C_2$ | $(\tfrac58,\tfrac{3}{16})$ |
| $P_2$ | $B_1B_2 \cap C_3C_1$ | $(\tfrac{9}{20},\tfrac{1}{10})$ |
| $P_3$ | $B_2B_3 \cap C_1C_2$ | $(\tfrac{9}{20},\tfrac{9}{20})$ |
| $P_4$ | $B_2B_3 \cap C_2C_3$ | $(\tfrac{3}{16},\tfrac58)$ |
| $P_5$ | $B_3B_1 \cap C_2C_3$ | $(\tfrac{1}{10},\tfrac{9}{20})$ |
| $P_6$ | $B_3B_1 \cap C_3C_1$ | $(\tfrac{3}{16},\tfrac{3}{16})$ |

**Verification of one point.** $P_1$: on $B_1B_2$ at $t=\tfrac34$: $(\tfrac14+\tfrac38,\tfrac{3}{16})=(\tfrac58,\tfrac{3}{16})$ ✓; on $C_1C_2$ at $s=\tfrac14$: $(\tfrac34-\tfrac18,\tfrac{3}{16})=(\tfrac58,\tfrac{3}{16})$ ✓.

**Tracing the hexagon.** The boundary alternates between edges of the two triangles. Going around:
$$P_1 \xrightarrow{C_1C_2} P_3 \xrightarrow{B_2B_3} P_4 \xrightarrow{C_2C_3} P_5 \xrightarrow{B_3B_1} P_6 \xrightarrow{C_3C_1} P_2 \xrightarrow{B_1B_2} P_1$$

**Area via the Shoelace formula.** With vertices in this cyclic order:

$$\text{Area}=\tfrac12\left|\sum (x_i y_{i+1}-x_{i+1}y_i)\right|$$

Computing each consecutive pair (all over denominator $320$):

- $P_1P_3$: $\tfrac58\cdot\tfrac{9}{20}-\tfrac{9}{20}\cdot\tfrac{3}{16}=\tfrac{90-27}{320}=\tfrac{63}{320}$
- $P_3P_4$: $\tfrac{9}{20}\cdot\tfrac58-\tfrac{3}{16}\cdot\tfrac{9}{20}=\tfrac{90-27}{320}=\tfrac{63}{320}$
- $P_4P_5$: $\tfrac{3}{16}\cdot\tfrac{9}{20}-\tfrac{1}{10}\cdot\tfrac58=\tfrac{27-20}{320}=\tfrac{7}{320}$
- $P_5P_6$: $\tfrac{1}{10}\cdot\tfrac{3}{16}-\tfrac{3}{16}\cdot\tfrac{9}{20}=\tfrac{6-27}{320}=-\tfrac{21}{320}$
- $P_6P_2$: $\tfrac{3}{16}\cdot\tfrac{1}{10}-\tfrac{9}{20}\cdot\tfrac{3}{16}=\tfrac{6-27}{320}=-\tfrac{21}{320}$
- $P_2P_1$: $\tfrac{9}{20}\cdot\tfrac{3}{16}-\tfrac58\cdot\tfrac{1}{10}=\tfrac{27-20}{320}=\tfrac{7}{320}$

$$\text{Sum}=\frac{63+63+7-21-21+7}{320}=\frac{98}{320}$$

$$[\text{hexagon}]=\frac12\cdot\frac{98}{320}=\frac{49}{320}$$

**Final fraction.** Since $[A_1A_2A_3]=\tfrac12$:

$$\frac{[\text{common part}]}{[A_1A_2A_3]}=\frac{49/320}{1/2}=\boxed{\dfrac{49}{160}}$$
